title: Whole Numbers: Prime Factors, HCF and LCM of Three Numbers, and Ratio
seo_title: Grade 8 Whole Numbers Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Use prime factorisation of numbers to find LCM and HCF; solve problems in contexts involving ratio, rate and direct and indirect proportion.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 8 whole numbers worksheets: prime factorisation, HCF and LCM, ratio and direct and inverse proportion. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Prime factors give the HCF and the LCM.
key_sub: Inverse proportion: one up, the other down.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Write each number as a product of primes: 72 = 2³ × 3².
  • HCF: the primes the numbers share, with the smallest powers. LCM: every prime, with the biggest powers.
  • Ratio: add the parts, find one part, then multiply.
  • Direct proportion: both go up together. Inverse proportion: one goes up as the other goes down.

Examples

Example

HCF and LCM of 12, 18 and 30

12 = 2² × 3

18 = 2 × 3²

30 = 2 × 3 × 5

Answer: HCF 6, LCM 180

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Composite factorsKeep breaking down until all factors are prime.
HCF or LCM?HCF is small; LCM is big.
Inverse as directMore workers take less time.

faq.q: How do I find the LCM of 3 numbers?
faq.a: Use every prime factor with its highest power.

items.q: Write 180 as a product of prime factors in index form.
items.e: Divide by primes: 2 appears 2 times, 3 appears 2 times, 5 appears 1 time. So 180 = 22 × 32 × 5.

items.q: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 6 and 8.
items.e: Factors of 6: 1, 2, 3, 6. Factors of 8: 1, 2, 4, 8. The biggest number in both lists is 2.

items.q: Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 18 and 12.
items.e: Multiples of 18: 18, 36, … The first one that is also a multiple of 12 is 36. (18 × 12 = 216 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.)

items.q: A bag of sweets is shared equally. With 3 children, each gets 20 sweets. How many would each get with 5 children?
